stack-S0-framework-data-access.recommendation: PROPOSAL for the owner to approve through an ADR. Use Next.js 16.x App Router on the Node.js runtime only. Put all DB access in a separate server-only Data Access Layer (DAL) module per privacy domain, and expose privacy-relevant operations as explicit Route Handlers. React Router v8 is the close alternative if hosting is Cloudflare Workers or the owner prefers an explicit request/response model. For data access, use Drizzle ORM with one instance, pool, Postgres LOGIN role and secret per domain. Write all security DDL (roles, GRANTs, ENABLE+FORCE RLS, policies, SECURITY DEFINER functions) as hand-written SQL migrations alongside drizzle-kit generated ones, and assert it in CI against a Postgres 18 container. Validate with Zod 4. Kysely is the fallback; Prisma is not recommended for design A.

options.name: Next.js 16.4 App Router
options.verdict: Recommended (proposal). Most mainstream (20.6% in Stack Overflow 2026), official DAL guidance, `server-only` build errors, best React a11y ecosystem, stable Adapter API. Watch for: Server Actions are hidden POST endpoints, a record of critical RSC CVEs (another patch due 2026-10-14), and unit tests can't cover async Server Components.

options.name: React Router v8 framework mode
options.verdict: Close alternative. Every loader/action is an explicit, testable URL, and `.server` modules fail the build if they reach client code. Native Vercel/Cloudflare/Node support and the least lock-in, but much less mainstream (Remix 1.7%).

options.name: SvelteKit 3
options.verdict: Not recommended now. Released 2026-10-01 with breaking changes. Remote functions not yet stable. Server-only checks are disabled when TEST=true. Thinner a11y component ecosystem.

options.name: Django 6.1 (chosen over Rails/Laravel)
options.verdict: Credible third. Best built-in support for per-alias DB credentials, refuses cross-database foreign keys, mature tests, allauth covers OIDC and SAML. Vercel now runs it as one function. Weaker polished interactive UI, contrib.admin is a §3 hazard, and Workers support is unverified.

options.name: Drizzle ORM (0.45.4 stable; v1 RC)
options.verdict: Recommended. Declares RLS policies and roles; GRANTs and SECURITY DEFINER functions go in --custom SQL migrations. Its logger receives query params, so it must stay off in production. Re-check v1 status at ADR time.

options.name: Prisma 8
options.verdict: Not recommended for design A. The schema can't express RLS, roles or grants, and the only documented RLS pattern is a per-query batch-transaction example 'not intended to be used in production'.

options.name: Kysely 0.29.6
options.verdict: Best alternative: SQL-first, hand-written migrations with a DB-level lock, and Better Auth's built-in adapter. Still pre-1.0.

options.name: Raw postgres.js / node-postgres
options.verdict: Use as the driver under Drizzle or Kysely, not on its own (weak result typing). postgres.js has a single maintainer.

options.name: Atlas migrations
options.verdict: Policies, roles/permissions and functions require paid Atlas Pro, so not suitable for the privacy-critical DDL on a <$5/month budget.

risks: Next.js RSC / Server Actions add a large attack surface with a history of critical CVEs, so patching within days is mandatory (next update scheduled 2026-10-14).

Within a single deployment every server module can read every env var. DB-role separation is enforced by Postgres, but secret separation per code path is only by convention unless services are deployed separately.
A session-level SET (instead of SET LOCAL) behind a transaction-mode pooler could leak one request's context to another; needs a CI ban and integration tests.
Unverified gotcha: placeholder GUCs may read back as '' rather than NULL on reused connections; policies must use nullif() and be tested behind the pooler.
ORM query loggers (Drizzle receives params), framework error logs and Sentry defaults can put identity and anonymous text in the same log, breaching §3/§6.2.
Unique constraints or FKs used for upvote de-duplication can leak existence through RI checks that bypass RLS.
Vendor RLS helpers (Neon auth.user_id(), Supabase roles) would lock policies to one provider.
Drizzle v1 is still a release candidate and changes the migrations folder layout; whether drizzle-kit push would drop custom-SQL policies is unverified.
Claude's training data may lag the fresh releases (SvelteKit 3, React Router v8, Next 16.4, Prisma 8), so versioned docs must be consulted.
Per-domain pools multiply DB connections under serverless bursts (e.g. a 1,000-student class); free-tier pooler limits must be checked by the hosting branch.

privacy-A-db-enforced.recommendation: Proposal for the owner to approve, not a decision. Use one Postgres database with a schema per §6.1 domain. Questions and comments carry no author column. Per-student counters are keyed by pid = HMAC(K_c, user_id) in locked schemas. De-duplication (upvote, follow, report, unclear) uses per-item tags HMAC(K_c, label‖user‖item), with merges de-duplicated by iterating the roster. The course key is stored wrapped: Supabase Vault (K2), or portably under an app-held key (K3). Every privacy-relevant action goes through whitelisted SECURITY DEFINER functions that resolve the caller from a session secret. The Supabase/Neon Data API stays off, and catalog-level tests run in CI. Start with synchronous crediting (Mode S) and keep the client-token deferred mode (Mode D) as a no-migration upgrade. Mode S's xmin side channel is an operator-level limitation to be documented. The operator and vendors stay inside the trust boundary.

options.name: (i) Keyed pseudonym pid = HMAC(K_c, user_id) with wrapped K_c
options.verdict: Recommended. A logical DB dump cannot link counters or tags to students without the unwrap key. Destroying K_c crypto-shreds everything at once. Rotating the key costs one pass over the roster.

options.name: (ii) Random per-(student, course) pseudonym in a locked linkage table
options.verdict: Viable, but the linkage table sits in clear in any dump unless it is also encrypted. Tags still need a key, so it doesn't remove the need for key custody.

options.name: (iii-a) One per-course pseudonym stored on upvote/follow rows
options.verdict: Rejected. Merging is trivial, but one pid links all of a student's upvotes and follows and joins straight to the counters (cross-item profiling).

options.name: (iii-b) Per-item tags HMAC(K_c, label||user||item)
options.verdict: Recommended. Tags can't be linked across items without the key. Merges de-duplicate by testing each roster member inside the definer function, about 2N HMACs.

options.name: K1 raw course key in a locked table
options.verdict: Rejected. Anyone with a dump gets the key, which recreates the §12 'reversible hash' problem.

options.name: K2 Supabase Vault / K3 KEK-wrapped key passed as a bind parameter / K4 KMS-held KEK for production
options.verdict: K3 for portability, or K2 if the stack is Supabase. K4 is the production upgrade. Do not use pgsodium: Supabase marks it pending deprecation.

options.name: Mode S: synchronous crediting in the same transaction
options.verdict: Prototype default. Simple, and it guarantees integrity. Weakness: the content row and counter row share xmin, so the operator, the DB vendor or anyone with a physical backup can attribute each student's latest action. Ordinary queries can't.

options.name: Mode D: deferred crediting via a client-held one-time credit token
options.verdict: Upgrade path with no data migration. Closes the logical xmin link. Costs: credit appears late, and tokens can be lost (cleared storage, device switch).

options.name: Variant A-prime: Supabase Data API with RLS and auth.uid()
options.verdict: Not recommended. Gateway logs index the JWT subject and request path for every RPC, RLS becomes internet-facing, and it locks the design to Supabase.

key_claims.claim: PostgreSQL grants EXECUTE on new functions to PUBLIC by default. SECURITY DEFINER functions should set search_path with pg_temp last, and privileges should be revoked and granted in the same transaction that creates the function. LEAKPROOF can only be set by a superuser.
Superusers and BYPASSRLS roles always bypass RLS. Table owners bypass it unless FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is set. With RLS enabled and no matching policy, access is denied by default.
xmin is the transaction ID of the inserting transaction for each row version, and ctid is the row's physical location. Both are system columns that any role with SELECT on the table can read.
track_commit_timestamp defaults to off and can only be set at server start.

By default, failing statements are logged (log_min_error_statement = ERROR) but their bind parameters are not (log_parameter_max_length_on_error = 0). If statement logging is turned on, bind parameters are logged in full (log_parameter_max_length = -1).
PG 18 offers gen_random_uuid()/uuidv4() and uuidv7(). uuid_extract_timestamp() recovers the timestamp from v1 and v7 UUIDs.
RFC 9562: UUIDv7 embeds a 48-bit Unix millisecond timestamp. UUIDs MUST NOT be used as security capabilities, and v4 is recommended for security-related contexts.
pgcrypto provides hmac() and gen_random_bytes() (at most 1024 bytes per call). Data and keys pass in clear between client and server, so TLS is needed and the DB administrator must be trusted.

On Supabase, postgres is the default table owner and has bypassrls. Views bypass RLS by default unless created with security_invoker (PG15+). SECURITY DEFINER functions should use search_path = '' and must not live in exposed schemas.
The Supabase Data API can be disabled entirely. On existing projects, tables in the public schema get default grants to anon, authenticated and service_role.
Supabase's new default (tables not automatically exposed to the Data API) applies to new projects from 2026-05-30 and to all existing projects on 2026-10-30.
Supabase Vault encrypts secrets with authenticated encryption (AEAD) under a per-project root key that is never stored in the database. Restore-to-new-project and branching copy that key.
Supabase lists pgsodium as pending deprecation, does not recommend it, and says to use Vault instead.
Supabase API Gateway logs can be filtered by JWT subject (user ID) and request pathname.

Supabase Free: $0, 500 MB database, 2 active projects, paused after 1 week of inactivity, no backups or PITR, 1-day API/DB log retention, 1-hour auth audit logs. Pro starts at $25/month with daily backups kept 7 days.

Neon allows CREATE ROLE via SQL (500 roles per branch). Roles created in the Console, CLI or API join neon_superuser, which has BYPASSRLS (projects after 2023-08-15) and pg_read_all_data. Roles created via SQL do not join it.
Neon Free: $0, 1 GB per project, 100 CU-hours per project, scale-to-zero after 5 minutes, 6-hour restore window. The Launch plan offers up to 7 days of history.
The Neon Data API is opt-in per branch, and authorization relies entirely on Postgres GRANTs and RLS.
Vercel runtime logs record request path, search params, user agent and time. Retention is 1 hour on Hobby and 1 day on Pro.
In Supabase, track_commit_timestamp is a CLI-only setting, and supautils lets the postgres role change log_statement and log_min_duration_statement.

Privacy Pass (RFC 9576, with RFC 9578 for issuance and RFC 9577 for the HTTP scheme) provides tokens that cannot be linked to their issuance. This is cited only as a cross-family alternative for survey de-duplication.
A pg_dump/COPY export follows physical row order, so rows written together line up across tables. Mitigating this with CLUSTER and fillfactor is a proposal.

new_open_questions: NQ-A1: Who receives 'Answer posted': followers, the asker, or both? Notifying the asker requires storing an asker tag, which weakens the no-author-data property.
NQ-A2: May students view, edit or delete their own anonymous posts? Any of these needs a stored authorship capability.
NQ-A3: Can a student withdraw an upvote, and if so, does 'upvotes given' go down?
NQ-A4: May students upvote their own question? Blocking it requires author data.
NQ-A5: Does hiding or deleting content take away participation credit already earned? Family A can only do this by adding an encrypted author reference, a design fork to settle before the Q9 ADR.
NQ-A6: When questions are merged, does a student who upvoted both keep 2 'upvotes given'? What happens to the merged-away question's answers and 'Still unclear' marks, and who can see unclear counts?

NQ-A7: How are level aggregates protected from differencing against the shared-results list? Options: hide them once the sharing window opens, apply a complex suppression rule, add noise, or drop the aggregate.
NQ-A8: What timestamp precision is stored and shown for content? Finer precision makes timing correlation easier; coarser precision weakens the 'most recent' sort.
NQ-A9: Is the platform operator (the owner) inside the trust boundary for the prototype, and for production?
NQ-A10: Is delayed crediting (Mode D) acceptable from a UX standpoint, given that it closes the xmin side channel?
NQ-A11: May the moderation log or dashboards record or show staff identity next to content? Does 'identity-bearing' in §3 include staff?
NQ-A12: How should repeat anonymous abusers be handled? Options: moderation only, sanction without revealing identity, or the §6.4 exceptional process.
NQ-A13: Does asking a question automatically follow it?
NQ-A14: Must the exit survey prevent duplicate submissions?
NQ-A15: Is a shared level frozen when the student shares, or live until the instructor finalises?
NQ-A16: Which vendor logs are acceptable, and must we verify they contain no request bodies (e.g. Supabase gateway)?
NQ-A17: Can one person be both a TA and a student in the same course?
NQ-A18: Should presentation mode and analytics show live totals or snapshots? Live totals create a classroom-observation side channel.
risks: Mode S: the content row and the counter row share xmin, so the operator, the DB vendor or anyone with a physical backup can attribute each student's most recent credited action. Ordinary queries cannot; this must be documented as a limitation.

The operator holds both the database and the unwrap key (KEK), so they can test every roster member against the upvote, follow and report tags until the course key is shredded. Backups keep the key until they expire (Supabase Pro: 7 days; Neon Free: 6 hours).
Comparing the level-distribution aggregate with the shared-results list can reveal non-sharers' levels unless aggregates are hidden or restricted (NQ-A7).

Supabase defaults: postgres has bypassrls and owns tables by default, and the Data API grant change reaches existing projects on 2026-10-30. Misconfiguration exposes schemas. Mitigate by disabling the Data API, using a custom owner role with FORCE RLS, and running a CI probe.
Neon: any role created in the Console joins neon_superuser (BYPASSRLS plus pg_read_all_data). The app must use roles created via SQL only.
Turning on statement logging (log_statement or log_min_duration_statement) logs bind parameters in full. That would put session tokens and post text together in DB logs.

With no author data stored, credit cannot be revoked, repeat abusers cannot be sanctioned, self-upvotes cannot be blocked, and posts cannot be edited. Each can only be added going forward, and each weakens the core property.

If the app server is fully compromised (all secrets, including cc_auth), the attacker can mint sessions and query the stored per-student state (upvotes, follows, counts) for every user, and can log future posts with their authors.
Business logic in PL/pgSQL plus strict grant discipline on every migration raises maintenance risk for a solo developer. The catalog-invariant CI tests are the main mitigation.
Several mitigations rely on Postgres behaviours I haven't verified: dump row order, HOT updates under fillfactor, CLUSTER's effect on xmin. Each needs an empirical test before anyone relies on it.

stack-H1H2-vercel.recommendation: PROPOSAL for owner approval: for the prototype, use H2a. That is Next.js on Vercel with functions pinned to yul1 (Montréal), plus Supabase Free in ca-central-1 used only as managed Postgres (Data API disabled, one custom login role per data domain, in-app auth library). This keeps the Canadian option open, avoids Neon's compute-hours cliff and gives the best local dev. Switch to H1 (Vercel iad1 + Neon aws-us-east-1) if the privacy design needs 3 or more physically separate databases (design B) and US hosting is acceptable. Never use Supabase's client-side Data API for anonymous content. Either way, the owner must first confirm eligibility for Vercel Hobby's non-commercial clause or budget Vercel Pro at $20/month, which by itself breaks the $5 target.

options.name: H1: Vercel Hobby + Neon Free + in-app auth (Better Auth)
options.verdict: About $1/mo (domain only) if under 100 CU-hours/project. Best fit for privacy design B: 100 free projects, each with its own credentials and quota. No Canadian Neon region, and the region can't be changed later. The free tier suspends compute until next month at the cap; my estimate is 89–134 CU-h at the assumed scale. The neon_superuser role has BYPASSRLS and read-all. Preview branches copy production data by default. Choose it when design B and US hosting are acceptable.

options.name: H1-NA: H1 with Neon Auth (managed Better Auth)
options.verdict: Not recommended. The page mentions only email/password and Google OAuth (no SAML or OIDC for UW SSO), and it ties identity to the vendor.

options.name: H2a: Vercel + Supabase Free as plain Postgres, Data API disabled, in-app auth
options.verdict: PROPOSED for the prototype. About $1/mo. Compute and database can both run in Canada (yul1 + ca-central-1). Free compute is always on with no meter. Over-quota handling starts with a grace period, though it is still an outage risk afterwards. Excellent local dev. Weaknesses: 500 MB database, only 2 free projects (design B limited), no backups on Free (do your own db dump), pauses after 1 week idle.

options.name: H2b: H2a but with Supabase Auth used server-side
options.verdict: Workable but riskier for §6.1. auth.users sits in the same database as content, the dashboard runs as postgres, and auth_logs record email, user ID and IP. It gives a SAML path on Pro ($25 + $0.015 per SSO MAU after 50). Needs custom SMTP: the built-in email allows only 2 messages per hour, to team members only.

options.name: H2c: Supabase Auth + client-side Data API/PostgREST with RLS (PDF chat pattern)
options.verdict: Not recommended for anonymous content, upvotes, participation or survey. RLS tends to need auth.uid() on content rows, and gateway logs record end-user IP, precise geolocation and path. The logs UI also lets you filter by JWT subject, so log lines can be tied to user IDs. Highest lock-in.

new_open_questions: PQ-1: Is Canadian data residency required for production, and for a pilot with real UW users? (Neon has no CA region and its regions are immutable.)
PQ-2: Is anyone paid to build or run ClearCourse AI, or is commercialisation intended? (This decides Vercel Hobby eligibility.)
PQ-3: Must a DPA or institutional privacy review be in place before real student data is used? (The Vercel DPA, as written, covers only Pro and Enterprise.)

PQ-4: Do database backups and dumps count as 'exports' under §6.2/§3, since a full dump puts identity and content together? Where may they be stored, encrypted with which keys, and kept for how long? (Relates to Q17.)
PQ-5: How should hosting-platform request logs (IP, user agent, path, timestamp) be treated under §6.2, and what retention is acceptable? (These logs must go in the threat model, Q8.)
PQ-6: Must presentation mode and voting update live, or is periodic or manual refresh acceptable? (§7.8 is silent; the answer drives cost.)
PQ-7: What availability and latency does 'polished and credible' (§8) require? (This decides whether cold starts and pause-after-idle are acceptable.)
PQ-8: May AI coding agents access production data or logs, for example via MCP?
PQ-9: Must preview and staging environments use only synthetic data? (Neon branches copy production data by default.)
PQ-10: What is the expected pilot scale (courses, students, largest course)? A single 1,000-student course exceeds both free tiers.
risks: Vercel Hobby's non-commercial clause: a university pilot, or a paid builder, may count as commercial. That would force Pro at $20/mo and break the $5 target. This is an interpretation I could not verify.
Neon Free compute-hours cliff: compute stays suspended until the next billing period. My estimate at the assumed scale is 89–134 CU-h/month against a cap of 100.
Supabase Free has no automated backups. A do-it-yourself dump is needed, and a full dump puts identity and content in one artifact.
Supabase Free pauses after 1 week of inactivity, which would take the site down between terms until the owner clicks restore.
The Supabase client-side Data API pattern (H2c) lets vendor logs and RLS design link users to content. This conflicts with §6.2.

Operator consoles see everything: Neon's neon_superuser has BYPASSRLS and read-all; the Supabase dashboard runs as postgres. Design A alone cannot stop the owner or an operator joining tables, so a key held outside the database, or design B, is needed.
Vercel request logs (IP, user agent, path, query string) can correlate sign-in and content-posting requests. This is a limitation of anonymity that must be documented.

Vercel env vars cannot be limited to individual functions, so credential separation inside one Vercel project relies on code discipline only. Real separation needs separate Vercel projects and signed internal APIs.
Magic-link sign-in on a free email tier is fragile: 100/day at Resend, and Supabase custom SMTP defaults to 30/hour. A class start could exceed these.
A 1,000-student course exceeds both free tiers: Vercel CPU and invocations, Supabase Realtime's 200 connections, and email caps.
Preview deployments with Neon branches would get copies of real student data, and Vercel-managed cleanup can lag for months.

Several facts are Unverified or conflicting: Supabase's definition of inactivity, its restore window, whether gateway logs carry JWT subjects, Vercel Pro's region count, and real cold-start latencies. A measured spike is recommended.

auth-A1-prototype-signin.recommendation: PROPOSAL for the owner to approve; nothing here is decided. If Q3 picks TypeScript, use Better Auth (MIT, v1.7.7 or later) with database sessions kept in the identity schema. The always-available sign-in is a 6-digit email one-time code limited to admin-configured domains (default proposal: uwaterloo.ca); avoid clickable magic links because mail scanners can use them up before the user clicks. Add 'Sign in with Microsoft', pinned to the UW tenant and keyed on (tid, oid), only if a free 1-2 hour spike (S1) shows ordinary UW users can consent without admin approval. Link accounts on (issuer, subject) only, never by email, and keep impersonation turned off. Note on the run itself: this branch did not hang. A complete first pass already existed (written 21:03), so this re-run only closed two remaining Unverified items instead of repeating the research.

options.name: Entra ID multi-tenant OIDC (Sign in with Microsoft), authority pinned to UW tenant 723a5a87-...
options.verdict: Conditional yes. Strongest proof of UW affiliation (tenant membership, not role) and best path to production, because oid stays the same for any later UW-sanctioned app. UW's user-consent setting is not public. A solo developer cannot get publisher verification (it needs a legally registered business in the Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program). privacy-B-separated-services.recommendation: PROPOSAL for the owner, not a decision. Use Family B's principles whatever platform is chosen: never store the author, use per-item keyed HMAC tags for upvotes, follows and reports, credit participation through stateless signed receipts with delayed, batched, idempotent processing, and send emails with no content. judge-stack.recommendation: This is a proposal for the owner to approve through an ADR. It closes no open question. Recommended prototype stack: TypeScript with Next.js 16.x App Router on the Node.js runtime only, following S0's privacy-domain DAL rules, with no proxy.ts and pinned to a release that includes the 2026-10-14 out-of-band security fix. Drizzle ORM with one instance, pool, LOGIN role and secret per privacy domain. Migrations use drizzle-kit generate plus hand-written SQL for every role, grant, FORCE RLS policy and SECURITY DEFINER function. They are applied only from GitHub Actions, and CI checks them with catalogue assertions. Database: Supabase Free in ca-central-1, used only as plain Postgres (Data API disabled, default grants revoked, no Supabase Auth, SDK or Vault). Host: Vercel Hobby with functions pinned to yul1, but only if the owner confirms that Hobby's "non-commercial personal use" rule fits and that no DPA is needed for the prototype (PQ-J2/PQ-J3). Pre-agreed fallback (H4-CA): the same app as a container on Cloud Run northamerica-northeast1 with the same Supabase database. Auth input to Q4: Better Auth with database sessions and email one-time codes. Email integration point: a content-free mailer port inside the identity domain, using Amazon SES ca-central-1 on an AWS Paid-plan account, because Free-plan accounts close after 6 months. Domain: Porkbun .ca if eligible, else .com. CI: GitHub Actions on a personal repo, running a Postgres service container, migrations, catalogue assertions, Vitest, Playwright plus axe, and a docker build. Estimated prototype cost is about USD 1.12–1.17 (about CAD 1.60–1.67) per month. A pilot costs about USD 27–47 and lean production about USD 52–62 (USD 152–162 with PITR). Scores out of 100: H2 78.5, H4 77.5, H3b 70.5, H1 70.0, H3a 62.0. H4 is the most robust: it wins if Vercel Hobby can't be used, if a DPA is required, or if the owner wants operator-proof privacy.

ranking.option: H2 (H2a): Next.js on Vercel Hobby yul1 + Supabase Free ca-central-1 used as plain Postgres
ranking.rationale: Weighted 78.5/100. About USD 1.17/month. The only free managed Postgres in the inputs with a Canadian region. Full support for family A; lowest lock-in when used as plain Postgres; most mainstream DX. Weaknesses: Vercel Hobby's non-commercial clause and missing DPA, up to 30-day lockout at caps, Supabase Free pauses after a week idle and has no backups, family B is weak at $0 (2 projects).

ranking.option: H4 (H4-CR / H4-CA): Next.js standalone container on Google Cloud Run + Supabase or Neon Postgres
ranking.rationale: Weighted 77.5; never below 75.5 in any sensitivity scenario. Supports families A and B fully, has the lowest lock-in, and offers Canadian compute and DB. The GCP terms show no non-commercial clause. Costs: cold starts, GCP/IAM complexity, possible automatic overage billing (alerts-only budgets don't cap; spend-cap eligibility for Cloud Run Unverified), and a custom domain in Canada needs Firebase Hosting or a load balancer at an Unverified price. Wins scenarios S1 (Hobby ineligible or DPA needed) and S3 (operator-proof B-full).

ranking.option: H3b: Cloudflare Workers (React Router v8) + Hyperdrive + Postgres
ranking.rationale: Weighted 70.5. Keeps Postgres for family A, with platform-enforced per-Worker secrets for B. The Cloudflare DPA is part of the self-serve agreement, and limits are hard daily stops with no surprise bills. But Next.js is only beta (vinext) or community (OpenNext) here. The Free 10 ms CPU limit is unmeasured, so Paid at USD 5.97 (above target) is likely. No Canadian compute; Neon has no Canadian region.

ranking.option: H1: Next.js on Vercel Hobby + Neon Free (aws-us-east-1)
ranking.rationale: Weighted 70.0. Strongest $0 support for family B (100 projects).
